Identify the semantic role of THETA and ETA in a NONMEM control stream

Source: R/nm_identify_parameters.R
nm_identify_parameters.Rd

Parses $THETA, $OMEGA, $PK and $ERROR of a control stream (or $PRED when there is no $PK) and links each THETA and ETA to the PK parameter(s) it acts on, with a semantic role: typical_value, covariate_effect, iiv_scale, residual_error, iiv or structural_other. Executable equations are the primary source; comments are only used as labels and consistency checks.

Usage

nm_identify_parameters(ctl, likely_pk_only = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

ctl

Path to a NONMEM control stream (.ctl). (Formerly file, still accepted with a warning.)

likely_pk_only

If TRUE (default), mapping_detail keeps only variables that look like PK parameters (CL, V, Q, KA, F, ALAG...). mapping_detail_all always keeps every variable.

...

Former argument name, accepted with a warning until version 1.0: file (now ctl).

Value

An object of class nm_parameter_map, a list with, among others: parameter_table (one row per PK parameter with its THETA/ETA by role; derived_from names the parameters of the table that a derived parameter is computed from, e.g. "V" for S2 = V or "CL, V" for KE = CL/V, and is NA for the others), mapping_detail and mapping_detail_all (one row per PK parameter / THETA or ETA association; depth is the number of assignment steps between the THETA/ETA and the parameter, 0 when it appears directly in its definition), residual_error, special_theta (THETAs of model event times MTIME(n) in $PK and of mixture probabilities P(n) in $MIX, with their role model_event_time or mixture_probability; they are not counted in unmapped_theta), theta, omega, omega_elements (variances and BLOCK covariances), unmapped_theta, unmapped_omega, missing_theta_declaration, missing_omega_declaration and label_substitutions (the labels replaced and their THETA(n)/ETA(n)/ERR(n) reference; empty for a standard control stream).

Details

Covariate effects are recognised in power, exponential, linear, saturable and conditional forms (e.g. (WT/70)**THETA(4), EXP(THETA(4)*WT), THETA(1)*(1 + THETA(4)*(WT-70)), C_RES/(THETA(4) + C_RES), IF(SEX.EQ.1) TVCL = TVCL*THETA(4), including IF ... THEN ... ELSE ... ENDIF blocks). A variable defined several times keeps the THETA/ETA of all its definitions. When a variable is only defined under conditions (e.g. IF(SEX.EQ.1) CL = THETA(1) / IF(SEX.EQ.0) CL = THETA(2)), the THETA of its first definition in the file is the reference (typical_value) and the others are covariate effects. A covariate is any data item declared in $INPUT that is not a NONMEM-defined item (ID, TIME, DV, AMT, MDV, EVID, CMT...), whatever its name; items dropped with =DROP are ignored. Without $INPUT, any symbol used in $PK but not defined there is taken as a data item.

Wings for NONMEM extended control streams, where model records use the labels of the $THETA, $OMEGA and $SIGMA comments (e.g. CL = POPCL*EXP(eta_cl)), are handled: such labels are first replaced by THETA(n), ETA(n) or ERR(n), as in nm_convert_ctl(). A label is replaced only if it is used but never assigned in a model record and is not a $INPUT item.

See also

nm_identify_directory(), nm_extract_runs()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- nm_identify_parameters("run.ctl")
x$parameter_table
x$mapping_detail
x$omega_elements
} # }
